annotations.title: Extract text and tables from a PDF

description: Extract text and tables from a born-digital PDF (one made by software: invoices, statements, reports, contracts, forms), page by page, in reading order, plus any tables found from the text layout as rows of cells. Scanned PDFs (images of pages) have no text layer and come back listed in pages_without_text: OCR is not supported. Set include_lines to also get each line with its position in PDF points from the bottom-left of the page as the viewer sees it, the same frame pdf_edit uses, so you can stamp text next to something you found. Up to 200 pages per call; pass pages to read a large document in parts. pdf_find_text searches for specific text. With tables_format xlsx the tables come back as one Excel workbook instead (one sheet per table, all cells text): written to output_path (a .xlsx file) when given, otherwise returned inline as an application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet resource (a workbook over 7 MB is never returned inline and needs output_path). The source PDF is never modified; output_path is only written with tables_format xlsx.

include_lines.description: Also return every line of text with x, y, width and font size in points. Default false (smaller output).

output_path.description: Only with tables_format xlsx: path of a .xlsx file to write the workbook to, inside the allowed directories (PDFOPS_ROOT, default the working directory); an existing file there is overwritten. Without it (as when running remotely) the workbook is returned inline as a resource for the client to save.

pages.description: Pages to read, 1-based: "1-3,5,8-". Default: all pages.

password.description: Password to open the input, only needed for a user-password PDF (owner-locked files with an empty user password open without it).

pdf_path.description: PDF source: a path to a .pdf file inside the allowed directories (PDFOPS_ROOT, default the working directory), an https:// URL, or a data:application/pdf;base64,… URI. A URL or data URI works when this server runs remotely (Smithery, hosted gateways), where local paths do not exist.

tables_format.description: csv adds a csv string (RFC 4180, CRLF line ends) to each table next to rows. xlsx instead returns one Excel workbook, one sheet per table ("Page 3 Table 1"), with a short summary (no text, lines or rows); every cell is a text string, never a formula, and numbers are not converted. xlsx fails with no_tables when the pages read have no table (if the read stopped early the error says so and names the pages value to continue with). Default json. In csv cell values are returned verbatim: a cell starting with = + - or @ can run as a formula if the CSV is opened in a spreadsheet, so sanitise before opening.

name: pdf_extract_text

bytes.description: Only with tables_format=xlsx: size of the workbook

cells_truncated.description: Only with tables_format=xlsx: a cell over 32,767 characters was cut

output_path.description: Only with tables_format=xlsx: absolute path written, when output_path was supplied

resource_uri.description: Only with tables_format=xlsx: where the workbook resource is attached, when output_path was omitted

truncated_by.description: Only with tables_format=xlsx and truncated: which cap stopped the read or cut the workbook
